messages:
Alice Chen: Quick note — I brought up a candidate reranker (rk-v2-q8) on the sparse-query holdout this morning. Initial NDCG@10 dropped ~3.8% vs prod for the short-tail cohort, but long queries look fine.
Ben Patel: Oof. Is this the PTQ branch or OPQ?
Alice Chen: PTQ-int8 on top of the distillation checkpoint (same seed). No OPQ. Command I ran: 
```
python -m eval.rerank --model rk-v2-q8 --holdout datasets/holdout_sparse.csv --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 2025 --batch 256 --kvpack True
```
Maria Gomez: Can you paste the exact cohort definition? I want to check sample overlap with training.
Alice Chen: Cohort = queries with term_count <= 3 OR char_len <= 30. We used stratified sampling by query_length and source.
Leo Tran: Did you rerun with tokenizer parity vs prod? We saw a tokenizer seed/clip mismatch cause tiny shifts before.
Alice Chen: Yep tokenizer = prod-tokenizer-v3 (same vocab). I double-checked token counts.
Ben Patel: How about candidate ordering? If you switched doc vs passage framing it can affect NDCG.
Alice Chen: Candidate generator is unchanged. I also re-evaluated using randomized candidate order to ensure metric isn't brittle — delta persists.
Maria Gomez: Do we have per-query delta distribution? 3.8% could be driven by a few high-impact queries.
Alice Chen: Uploading a quick bucketed diff now (attached as gist). Top-10 worst queries are mostly exact-match sparse queries where the new model prefers semantic matches.
Ben Patel: That suggests a calibration/score-scale change. Can you compare pairwise sigmoid/logit rescale?
Alice Chen: I tried simple rescale (multiply logits by 1.05) and NDCG recovered ~1.7% but not fully.
Leo Tran: Could be quantization bias on short contexts — int8 rounding can compress subtle logits. Try per-layer activation clipping/ema calibration.
Maria Gomez: Also check evaluation metric consistency: are we computing NDCG using the same gain function and cutoff? Prod uses linear gains and cutoff 10.
Alice Chen: Affirmed — same eval harness, same argparser flags. I also re-run with seed sweep [42,2025,777] — results stable across seeds.
Ben Patel: For rollout decision: can we split by traffic tier? Maybe keep rk-v2-q8 for long-form traffic where it improves recall and hold on short queries.
Maria Gomez: We should also test small prompt priming: append explicit query-scope token (e.g., "[SHORT]") to see if model reacts differently. That would be a signal it's a priming/LM preference rather than retrieval mismatch.
Alice Chen: Good call. I ran a quick priming probe: prefixing short queries with "[KW]" regained ~2.4% NDCG. So priming helps.
Leo Tran: Interesting — that implies score-shape is fine but model semantic preference changed. Could we keep quantization but inject a lightweight feature indicating query-type to reranker?
Ben Patel: Operationally, adding a query-type signal is low-risk. But we need to ensure feature extraction cost is acceptable.
Maria Gomez: For eval protocol change: propose adding a 'sparse-probe' holdout that we keep locked and require new models to pass within 1% NDCG delta before rollout. Also add priming experiment in the CI matrix.
Alice Chen: +1. I'll open a PR to add the holdout and a smokecheck that runs the priming probe automatically.
Eval Bot: Scheduled job eval-smoke-rerank started for rk-v2-q8 on holdout_sparse (run id: 20250315-09).
Ben Patel: Thanks. Also include a quick ablation: non-quantized rk-v2 vs rk-v2-q8 to measure quantization-only effect.
Alice Chen: Will do. Plan: 1) non-quant vs q8; 2) priming + q8; 3) feature-add probe. I'll post results by EOD. :thumbsup:
